content.comment_body: Hello, I have an application that appears well-suited for [product_name]. This application needs to switch 24VDC solenoids for pneumatic valves. The specifications are: power 5.4W, inrush current 10.9VA (0.091A), holding 7.7VA (0.064A), energize time 6ms, and de-energize time 2ms. Is it possible to use inductive loads like these with the SSR versions of [product_name]?

Hello, does SSR refer to Solid State Relay? If so, there may be a misunderstanding. Solid State Relays are not available for [product_name]. You can get mechanical relays in [product_name]. Detailed specifications are available in the manual. Visit [url] to access all information and download the manual for free. Hope this helps.

All versions of [product_name] without 'R' at the end of the name have transistor outputs. According to the manual (see page 252), the switching rate is 10 Hz for purely resistive loads and 0.5 Hz for inductive loads, which depends on the program cycle time. Additionally, when these modules are switched on, they provide a 1 signal at all outputs for 50ms, which should be considered for timing-sensitive applications.
Thank you for the responses and for referencing the relevant manual page with detailed information.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are clarifying whether [product_name] hardware can reliably switch small inductive loads, particularly 24VDC pneumatic solenoids, using solid state relays or transistor outputs. There was initial confusion about output types, but it was clarified that only mechanical relays or transistor outputs are available, not SSRs. It was also highlighted that transistor output versions have specific limitations, including restricted switching frequencies and an automatic 50ms signal when outputs are activated, which must be considered for applications where timing is critical.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] to reliably switch small inductive loads and want clear, documented information about output module options, especially regarding solid state relays or equivalents. They are looking for straightforward details about any limitations and capabilities when switching inductive loads.
